nmd_rule: PTC escapes NMD if located in the last exon or within 50 nt upstream of the last exon-exon junction (Nagy-Maquat 50-55nt rule)
DEUBAD_BAP1_binding_domain_aa: 240-360 (Pfam PF13919); N-terminal to junction; retained in every truncation from aa 361 onward
PHD_Cterminal_domain_aa: 2204-2246 (Pfam PF13922); in last exon; lost by essentially all truncating variants
interpretation: NMD-escaping ASXL3 truncations (PTC in distal exon 11 tip + all exon 12; ~55% of the ORF) are predicted to yield a stable-length protein that retains the DEUBAD/BAP1-binding domain but lacks the C-terminal PHD finger (and putative C-terminal degron). This is the same domain architecture that produces gain-of-function in truncated ASXL1 (PMID:26095772, 35122023, 34186160).
limitations: Computational prediction of NMD from transcript coordinates only; does not measure actual transcript/protein levels or functional activity. Does not incorporate patient-specific variant positions or minor transcripts. Requires wet-lab confirmation in ASXL3 patient material.
